source_text: Circa Felicitatem uero, et illi gratia domini eiusmodi contigit. Cum octo iam mensium uentrem haberet (nam praegnans fuerat adprehensa), instante spectaculi die in magno erat luctu, ne propter uentrem differretur (quia non licet praegnantes poenae repraesentari) et ne inter alios postea sceleratos sanctum et innocentem sanguinem funderet. Sed et commartyres grauiter contristabantur, ne tam bonam sociam quasi comitem solam in uia eiusdem spei relinquerent. Coniuncto itaque unito gemitu ad dominum orationem fuderunt ante tertium diem muneris. Et statim post orationem dolores inuaserunt. Et cum pro naturali difficultate octaui mensis in partu laborans doleret, ait illi quidam ex ministris cataractariorum: Quae sic modo doles, quid facies obiecta bestiis, quas contempsisti cum sacrificare noluisti? Et illa respondit: Modo ego patior quod patior; illic autem alius erit in me qui patietur pro me, quia et ego pro illo passura sum. Ita enixa est puellam, quam sibi quaedam soror in filiam educauit.
pass_a_gloss: But concerning Felicitas, grace of the Lord of this kind befell even her. Since she now had a belly of eight months, for she had been seized while pregnant, with the day of the show pressing on she was in great grief lest she be put off on account of the belly, because it is not permitted that pregnant women be presented for punishment, and lest afterwards among other criminals she pour out holy and innocent blood. But also her fellow-martyrs were gravely saddened lest they leave behind so good a companion as a comrade alone on the road of the same hope. Therefore with united groaning joined together they poured out prayer to the Lord before the third day of the games. And immediately after the prayer birth-pains seized her. And when, laboring in childbirth, she was in pain because of the natural difficulty of the eighth month, one of the attendants of the prison-warders says to her: You who suffer so now, what will you do when thrown to the beasts which you despised when you refused to sacrifice? And she answered: Now I suffer what I suffer; but there another will be in me who will suffer for me, since I too am about to suffer for him. Thus she bore a girl, whom a certain sister brought up for herself as a daughter.
pass_b_english: As for Felicitas, the grace of the Lord came to her in this manner. She was now eight months gone with child, for she had been arrested while pregnant, and as the day of the spectacle drew near she grieved deeply for fear her punishment would be delayed because of her womb, since pregnant women may not be put forward for execution, and for fear she would later shed holy and innocent blood among common criminals instead of with the rest. Her fellow martyrs were also deeply grieved at the thought of leaving so good a comrade behind alone on the way to the same hope. And so with one united groan they poured out prayer to the Lord three days before the games, and immediately after that prayer her labor pains came upon her.

She suffered in travail from the natural hardship of an eighth-month birth, and one of the prison attendants said to her, If you cry out now in your present pain, what will you do when you are thrown to the beasts you scorned by refusing to sacrifice. She answered, Now I endure what I endure, but there another will be in me who will endure for me, because I am about to endure for him. In this way she delivered a little girl, whom one of the sisters took and raised as her own daughter.

choices.why: ante tertium diem muneris with spectaculi die in context means the scheduled arena show, not a gift or duty
passive infinitive with poenae as purpose; legal reason given for deferral of pregnant women
minister with genitive plural in a prison birth scene points to subordinate jail staff present at labor
